title: Volume is 2× average can mean two very different things
author: Electrical_Waltz_888
selftext:
Imagine a stock has traded 300,000 shares by 10:30 am. It usually trades 1 million shares in a full session, but its average by 10:30 am is 150,000.

That’s 30% of a normal full day’s volume and 2× its normal volume **at that time of day**. Both numbers are right. They answer different questions.

If a rule says “enter on unusually high volume”, I’d pin down the comparison before testing: are we looking at a completed daily candle, a completed intraday candle, or cumulative volume up to the same time in previous sessions?

A prompt I’d use: “Rewrite this volume rule so the numerator, denominator and time cutoff are explicit. List what historical data I need to test it without using any volume that wasn’t available at the decision time.”

For intraday systems, do you compare cumulative volume at the same clock time, or use the volume of each completed bar?

I wrote *The Complete Guide to AI Powered Trading*  It includes worked examples and 50 reusable prompts for writing trading rules, questioning backtest results and reviewing trades with AI.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
For intraday I'd compare each completed bar to the average volume of that same bar over the last 20 or so sessions. So the 10:25 to 10:30 bar vs the usual 10:25 to 10:30 bar.

  
Cumulative-at-same-time works too, but it gets slow to react later in the day, since one big spike at the open keeps the ratio high for hours. Per-bar shows you when the volume is actually coming in.

  
Also worth skipping the first few minutes and the half days, they mess up the averages a lot.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: cumulative to the same clock time, every time. per-bar comparisons get wrecked by the open: the first bar carries the auction print and everything that queued overnight, so "this 5-min bar is 3x the last one" is true at 9:35 most days and tells you nothing. one catch with the cumulative version, half days and the session after a holiday need dropping from the baseline or it drifts.
